advances: For every admissible central-triangle corner of a finite-rank-two interior endpoint datum, this gives the coordinate-invariant exposed-corner inequality, and it applies the inequality cyclically when all three corners are admissible. It gives both the exact simultaneous non-rejection region of the three corner tests and a joint sufficient condition forcing at least one corner to close. The resulting strict exclusion set is open and nonempty, so the extension argument applies to a genuine parameter region rather than only to the single calibration in accepted fact `4c0351818e9f4eb3`. It does not by itself close the whole interior alternative: the accepted predecessors do not force all three endpoint hulls to have the required exposed corners, nor do they force the two marginal thresholds at any one corner.
author: mp_r68_rank2_three_corner_cover
proof:
Taking gradients in (1) gives
\[
\nabla f_1+\nabla f_2+\nabla f_3=0.
\tag{26}
\]
If one cyclic pair of gradients were dependent, (26) would put all three gradients in one line, contrary to the rank-two hypothesis. Thus every cyclic pair is independent. Moreover,
\[
\det(\nabla f_2,\nabla f_3)
=\det(\nabla f_3,\nabla f_1)
=\det(\nabla f_1,\nabla f_2),
\tag{27}
\]
so (2) is well defined and positive.

For fixed cyclic \((i,j,k)\), the affine map
\[
x\longmapsto(f_j(x),f_k(x))
\]
has absolute Jacobian \(J\). It sends \(\mathcal T\) bijectively to
\[
\{(s,t):s\leq0,\ t\leq0,\ s+t\geq-1\},
\]
whose area is \(1/2\), and sends \(O_i\) to \((0,0)\). This proves (3) and the assertions about the central triangle. For the normalization (4), accepted fact `ed22242313aecf82` gives
\[
\sum_i\alpha_i\phi_i=\sigma,
\qquad
\nabla\phi_i=n_i.
\]
Thus the functions in (4) satisfy (1), and their \((1,2)\)-Jacobian is the displayed value of \(J\). Formula (3) then reproduces exactly the triangle-area formula in that accepted fact.

By (5) and convexity, every \(B_i\) in (7) is contained in \(K\). Fix an admissible \(i\), and use the area-preserving affine coordinates
\[
s=\frac{f_j}{\sqrt J},
\qquad
t=\frac{f_k}{\sqrt J}.
\tag{28}
\]
The point \(O_i\) becomes the origin, while
\[
F_i=
\left(
-\frac{\mathsf A_i}{\sqrt J},
\frac{\mathsf B_i}{\sqrt J}
\right),
\qquad
E_i=
\left(
\frac{\mathsf C_i}{\sqrt J},
-\frac{\mathsf D_i}{\sqrt J}
\right).
\tag{29}
\]
Conditions (8), (9), and the two exterior-side assumptions are precisely the convex-extension hypotheses of accepted fact `4c0351818e9f4eb3` for the core \(B_i\), extension \(K\), and coordinate halfplanes \(H_j=\{s\leq0\}\), \(H_k=\{t\leq0\}\). In the notation of that fact, its two thresholds become
\[
\frac12
\frac{\mathsf A_i}{\sqrt J}
\frac{\mathsf B_i}{\sqrt J}
=\tau_{i,j},
\qquad
\frac12
\frac{\mathsf C_i}{\sqrt J}
\frac{\mathsf D_i}{\sqrt J}
=\tau_{i,k},
\]
and its corner coefficient becomes
\[
\frac{\mathsf A_i}{\sqrt J}
\frac{\mathsf D_i}{\sqrt J}
=\gamma_i.
\]
The added area and the two added marginals in that fact are exactly \(\delta_i,e_{i,j},e_{i,k}\). It therefore gives (14), and rearrangement gives (15).

Taking the logical complement of (15) at each admissible corner gives exactly the three disjunctions in (16). Equation (17) follows from \(B_i\subseteq K\). Accepted fact `29dfdfc94477e532` supplies the all-double crossing relation
\[
c_\ell=h-u_\ell-(m-x_\ell),
\]
while the common-hull identity of accepted fact `174b54e9843ef8fc` gives the second formula in (18). Substitution proves (19).

For the common-core corollary, choose an index \(i\) for which \(e_i\) is largest. Then
\[
e_j+e_k=E-e_i\leq\frac{2E}{3},
\qquad
4e_je_k\leq(e_j+e_k)^2\leq\frac{4E^2}{9}.
\tag{30}
\]
Apply (14) at this corner and use \(\gamma_i\geq\gamma\). Equivalently,
\[
\delta
\leq e_j+e_k+\frac{4e_je_k}{\gamma_i}
\leq\frac{2E}{3}+\frac{4E^2}{9\gamma},
\]
which is (20). Its contrapositive is (21). Also \(H_1\cup H_2\cup H_3=\mathbb R^2\), because three positive \(f_i\)-values cannot sum to \(-1\); hence every common-core extension satisfies the basic bound \(\delta\leq E\).

It remains to verify the rational nonemptiness example. Successive edge-vector determinants of the polygon (22) alternate between \(1/4\) and \(5/16\), so the displayed order is strictly convex. In the three cyclic coordinate pairs
\[
(f_2,f_3),\qquad(f_3,f_1),\qquad(f_1,f_2),
\]
the two neighbors of the corresponding central vertex are always
\[
F=\left(-\frac12,\frac14\right),
\qquad
E=\left(\frac14,-\frac34\right).
\tag{31}
\]
Every vertex of \(B\) satisfies \(f_i\geq-1\) for every \(i\). Therefore, at \(O_i\),
\[
f_j+f_k=-1-f_i\leq0
\]
throughout \(B\), proving (9). The determinant of \(F\) with a positive \(t\)-axis vector is negative, and
\[
\det\left(
\left(-\frac14,\frac34\right),
\left(S-\frac14,\frac34\right)
\right)
=-\frac{3S}{4}<0
\qquad(S>0),
\]
so the two positive coordinate rays are on the required exterior sides. Thus every corner is admissible. Here \(J=1\), and (31) gives (23). Finally,
\[
\frac{4(1/32)^2}{3/8}=\frac1{96},
\]
which proves (25). All inequalities in (13) and (25) are strict, so continuity gives an open excluded neighborhood. This completes the proof.
statement:
Let \(f_1,f_2,f_3\) be nonconstant affine functions on \(\mathbb R^2\) such that
\[
f_1+f_2+f_3=-1,
\qquad
\operatorname{span}\{\nabla f_1,\nabla f_2,\nabla f_3\}=\mathbb R^2.
\tag{1}
\]
Put
\[
H_i=\{f_i\leq0\},
\qquad
\mathcal T=H_1\cap H_2\cap H_3.
\]
For cyclic \((i,j,k)=(1,2,3),(2,3,1),(3,1,2)\), let \(O_i\) be the unique point satisfying
\[
f_j(O_i)=f_k(O_i)=0.
\]
Then \(f_i(O_i)=-1\), \(\mathcal T\) is the nondegenerate triangle with vertices \(O_1,O_2,O_3\), and
\[
J:=|\det(\nabla f_j,\nabla f_k)|
\tag{2}
\]
is positive and independent of the cyclic pair. Moreover,
\[
|\mathcal T|=\frac1{2J}.
\tag{3}
\]
This is exactly the normalization of the finite-rank-two triangle in accepted fact `ed22242313aecf82`: for its data one may take
\[
f_i=-\frac{\alpha_i\phi_i}{\sigma},
\qquad
J=\frac{\alpha_1\alpha_2|\det(n_1,n_2)|}{\sigma^2}.
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(B\subseteq K\) be nonempty two-dimensional compact convex polytopes and assume
\[
B\subseteq K,
\qquad
\mathcal T\subseteq K.
\tag{5}
\]
In the actual all-double setting of accepted facts `174b54e9843ef8fc` and `29dfdfc94477e532`, the intended endpoint core is
\[
B=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq K.
\tag{6}
\]
For each \(i\), put
\[
B_i=\operatorname{conv}(B\cup\{O_i\})\subseteq K.
\tag{7}
\]
Call the \(i\)-th corner admissible if \(O_i\) is a boundary vertex of \(B_i\), its adjacent exposed edges have other endpoints \(F_i,E_i\) ordered as
\[
[E_i,O_i],\ [O_i,F_i],
\]
and, in the coordinate pair \((f_j,f_k)\),
\[
f_j(F_i)<0<f_k(F_i),
\qquad
f_k(E_i)<0<f_j(E_i),
\tag{8}
\]
\[
B_i\cap\{f_j>0,\ f_k>0\}=\varnothing.
\tag{9}
\]
Also require the ray \(\{f_j=0,f_k>0\}\) to be on the exterior side of \([O_i,F_i]\), and the ray \(\{f_k=0,f_j>0\}\) to be on the exterior side of \([E_i,O_i]\).

At an admissible corner define
\[
\mathsf A_i=-f_j(F_i),\quad
\mathsf B_i=f_k(F_i),\quad
\mathsf C_i=f_j(E_i),\quad
\mathsf D_i=-f_k(E_i),
\tag{10}
\]
\[
\tau_{i,j}=\frac{\mathsf A_i\mathsf B_i}{2J},
\qquad
\tau_{i,k}=\frac{\mathsf C_i\mathsf D_i}{2J},
\qquad
\gamma_i=\frac{\mathsf A_i\mathsf D_i}{J}.
\tag{11}
\]
All quantities in (10) and (11) are positive. Put
\[
\delta_i=|K\setminus B_i|,
\qquad
e_{i,\ell}=|(K\setminus B_i)\cap H_\ell|
\quad(\ell=j,k).
\tag{12}
\]
If
\[
e_{i,j}<\tau_{i,j},
\qquad
e_{i,k}<\tau_{i,k},
\tag{13}
\]
then
\[
\boxed{\quad
\gamma_i(\delta_i-e_{i,j}-e_{i,k})
\leq4e_{i,j}e_{i,k}.
\quad}
\tag{14}
\]
Equivalently, the \(i\)-th corner closes whenever
\[
e_{i,j}<\tau_{i,j},\qquad
e_{i,k}<\tau_{i,k},\qquad
\delta_i>
e_{i,j}+e_{i,k}+\frac{4e_{i,j}e_{i,k}}{\gamma_i}.
\tag{15}
\]

Thus, when all three corners are admissible, the exact simultaneous escape region of these three tests is
\[
\boxed{\quad
\bigcap_{\mathrm{cyc}(i,j,k)}
\left(
\{e_{i,j}\geq\tau_{i,j}\}
\ \cup\
\{e_{i,k}\geq\tau_{i,k}\}
\ \cup\
\left\{
\delta_i\leq e_{i,j}+e_{i,k}
+\frac{4e_{i,j}e_{i,k}}{\gamma_i}
\right\}
\right).
\quad}
\tag{16}
\]
Here “escape region” means exactly the parameter set not rejected by these three applications of the exposed-corner lemma; it is not asserted to be sufficient for a convex extension. For unrestricted endpoint data, failure of admissibility at a corner is one additional geometric escape at that corner.

The quantities in (12) are directly computable from actual endpoint data. If
\[
c_\ell=|K\cap H_\ell|,
\]
then
\[
\delta_i=|K|-|B_i|,
\qquad
e_{i,\ell}=c_\ell-|B_i\cap H_\ell|.
\tag{17}
\]
In the all-double branch of accepted facts `174b54e9843ef8fc` and `29dfdfc94477e532`, the crossing identities give
\[
c_\ell=h-u_\ell-m+x_\ell,
\qquad
h=\frac{2(M-m-U-q-E_R)}3,
\tag{18}
\]
and hence
\[
e_{i,\ell}
=
\frac{2(M-m-U-q-E_R)}3-u_\ell-m+x_\ell
-|B_i\cap H_\ell|.
\tag{19}
\]

There is a useful genuinely cyclic corollary. Suppose the same core works at all three corners, so \(B_i=B\), \(\delta_i=\delta\), and \(e_{i,\ell}=e_\ell\). Assume all six strict threshold inequalities in (13), and set
\[
E=e_1+e_2+e_3,
\qquad
\gamma=\min_i\gamma_i.
\]
Every convex extension then satisfies
\[
\boxed{\quad
\delta\leq\frac{2E}{3}+\frac{4E^2}{9\gamma}.
\quad}
\tag{20}
\]
Consequently, at least one of the three corner inequalities closes whenever
\[
\delta>\frac{2E}{3}+\frac{4E^2}{9\gamma}.
\tag{21}
\]

The exclusion region is nonempty independently of the calibration in accepted fact `4c0351818e9f4eb3`. In coordinates
\[
f_2(u,v)=u,\qquad f_3(u,v)=v,\qquad f_1(u,v)=-1-u-v,
\]
let \(B\) be the rational hexagon with counterclockwise vertices
\[
(0,0),\
\left(-\frac12,\frac14\right),\
(-1,0),\
\left(-\frac34,-\frac12\right),\
(0,-1),\
\left(\frac14,-\frac34\right).
\tag{22}
\]
All three central vertices are admissible for this same core, and at every corner
\[
\tau_{i,j}=\frac1{16},
\qquad
\tau_{i,k}=\frac3{32},
\qquad
\gamma_i=\frac38.
\tag{23}
\]
The target values
\[
\delta=\frac3{32},
\qquad
e_1=e_2=e_3=\frac1{32}
\tag{24}
\]
satisfy the basic covering identity \(E=\delta\) and every threshold, but
\[
\delta=\frac9{96}>
\frac1{16}+\frac1{96}
=e_j+e_k+\frac{4e_je_k}{\gamma_i}
=\frac7{96}
\tag{25}
\]
at all three corners. Hence no convex extension of this core has the target values (24), and the same remains true on an open neighborhood of (24).
